title: Chromatic number

problem.name: Graph coloring and chromatic number
problem.statement_latex:
Given $G=(V,E)$, find the smallest $k$ admitting $c:V\to[k]$ such that $c(u)\neq c(v)$ for every edge $uv$. The decision variant supplies $k$ and asks for such a coloring. Colors represent mutually incompatible time slots, frequencies, or resources.
The unrestricted quantum comparison uses QRAM time and classical RAM time, while fixed-color CNF algorithms are measured in bit operations.
problem.statement_text: Given $G=(V,E)$, find the smallest $k$ admitting $c:V\to[k]$ such that $c(u)\neq c(v)$ for every edge $uv$. The decision variant supplies $k$ and asks for such a coloring. The unrestricted quantum comparison uses QRAM time and classical RAM time, while fixed-color CNF algorithms are measured in bit operations.

quantum.details_latex: Here $n=|V|$ and the number of colors is optimized without a fixed bound. The algorithm combines restricted-family preprocessing, maximal-independent-set enumeration and quantum minimum finding. Its table is accessed coherently in the QRAM model.

classical.headline_latex: $O^*(2^n)$, inclusion--exclusion over independent sets; $\operatorname{poly}(n+|E|)2^{O_q(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ for fixed $q$-colorability, Boolean tensor contraction.
classical.details_latex: The first bound computes the unrestricted chromatic number. For a fixed number $q$ of colors, one-hot vertex-color variables give $qn$ Boolean variables and fixed-width clauses for vertex and edge conditions, even on dense graphs. Exact counting and self-reduction recover a coloring in polynomial space. On sparse graphs the exponent becomes $O_q(n/\sqrt{\log n})$.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant for unrestricted chromatic number, based on amplitude amplification. Fixed-$q$ decision has the displayed subexponential classical comparator.

evidence.description_latex: Rigorous quantum upper bound with partial evidence relative to the general classical chromatic-number algorithm. The fixed-$q$ comparison follows the explicit bounded-width encoding.

hardware.description_latex: Polynomial active subset and color registers coexist with exponentially many coherently accessible preprocessing values. Useful instances require fault tolerance; fixed-$q$ decision and unrestricted optimization have different relevant time comparisons.

algorithm_items.content_latex: \href{https://arxiv.org/pdf/2311.08042}{Gaspers and Li, \emph{Quantum Algorithms for Graph Coloring and Other Partitioning, Covering, and Packing Problems} (ICALP 2024)}. Theorem 8 and the coloring construction following it; appendix Algorithms 1--3 give the preprocessing and recursive procedures. The preliminary covering formulation gives the classical inclusion--exclusion comparison.
